infra-context

Infrastructure map

Architecture, NFRs, backend, frontend, environments and CI/CD of the system under test.

Overview

Bunkai TMS is a single Next.js 15 (App Router, React 19, TypeScript) full-stack app in one repo (upex-bunkai-tms, monorepo shape reported by /qa, one workspace). Persistence, auth and row-level security are Supabase (Postgres 17.6). It deploys to Vercel; the REST API lives in the same app under app/api/v1/ and its OpenAPI document is generated from Zod schemas.

The MVP runs one Supabase project for local, staging and "production" and holds no real customer data (target AGENTS.md rule 20).

Architecture

Request path. middleware.ts refreshes the Supabase session cookie and redirects unauthenticated users away from the protected prefixes (/home, /projects, /onboarding, /settings, /activity); /login, /auth, /api/auth are public. API routes are wrapped by withApiHandler (lib/api/handler.ts), which declares an auth mode per route (auth: 'public' on /api/v1/health), emits a request id and a one-line JSON log.

Auth. Two credential classes reach the API: a Supabase cookie session and a Bearer personal access token (bk_pat_..., hashed, scoped; lib/api/pat.ts). The cron route uses a third class, a bearer CRON_SECRET. Sign-in methods listed by /qa: email plus password (primary), GitHub and Google OAuth, magic link. Endpoints under /api/v1/auth/: check-email, confirm, magic-link, resend, signin, signup.

Database at architecture level. Staging DB measured 2026-10-05 over the read-only role: 35 public tables, 90 RLS policies, 82 public functions; 87 migration files 0001-0088 in supabase/migrations/ (gaps at 0079 and 0080, one 0084a). Business writes go through RPC functions. Entities and state machines: bun run context:map business-data-context.

Cross-cutting. Idempotency-Key header support backed by an idempotency_keys table (lib/api/idempotency.ts); an error envelope (lib/api/error-envelope.ts); a route capability snapshot test guards that every route declares a capability.

NFR: security

  • RLS on workspace-scoped data: 90 policies across 35 public tables (staging, 2026-10-05).
  • Role model viewer / member / admin / owner per workspace; PATs cannot mint PATs (cookie session only).
  • Service-role key is server-only (import 'server-only' in lib/env.ts); public vars are NEXT_PUBLIC_* only.
  • Cron route requires a bearer secret; an unauthenticated variant is treated as a data-exfiltration path.
  • Read-only QA database role qa_inspector_ro through the session pooler (port 5432, sslmode=require), provisioned by scripts/provision-qa-roles.ts.

NFR: reliability and observability

  • Idempotent writes: same key and payload replays the stored response; same key with another payload returns 409; an in-flight duplicate returns 409.
  • Observability is limited to structured one-line JSON request logs on stdout (Vercel log capture) with a request id. No APM or error tracker found in dependencies.
  • Health probe: GET /api/v1/health returns {ok, service, env, ts} with HTTP 200 on staging (measured 2026-10-05).

Backend

No separate backend repo: route handlers in app/api/v1/ (about 30 resource folders: acceptance-criteria, atcs, auth, billing, bugs, environments, imports, invites, milestones, modules, notifications, projects, runs, search, test-plans, tests, tokens, user-stories, workspaces and more) call domain code in lib/<domain>/ and Supabase RPCs.

Environment variable slots

App runtime (names only): NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL, NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY, SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET, NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL, CRON_SECRET, RESEND_API_KEY, RESEND_DIGEST_FROM_EMAIL, Stripe and Atlassian slots as above. Tooling: DBHUB_* (host, port, database, user, password, type), SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN, QA_E2E_USER_EMAIL, QA_E2E_USER_PASSWORD. Real values live in the credentials Epic, never in the repo.

Database setup

Migrations are applied through the Supabase MCP apply_migration and recorded in the ledger described in supabase/migrations/README.md; never DDL via execute_sql. Regenerate DB types with bun run types:gen.

Commands (read the target package.json for the live list)

bun run dev          # local app on :3000
bun run typecheck    # tsc --noEmit
bun run openapi:gen / openapi:check / openapi:diff
bun test

Target rule 17: never run next build locally (it clobbers the dev server's .next/).

  • One Supabase project serves local, staging and "production": a write from any env lands in the same data. Treat staging tests as shared-state.
  • Secrets: .env locally (the QA repo launches agents with dotenv -o so .env wins over inherited vars), Vercel env scopes for the app, GitHub Actions secrets for the QA repo. A pointer to the credentials artifact (a Jira Epic) is on /qa; content is never copied here.
  • Monitoring: Vercel logs and Supabase dashboards only.
  • Rollback: not documented in the target repo; see discovery-gaps.

CI/CD

Target app. No .github/workflows directory in upex-bunkai-tms. Deploys are Vercel Git-integration deploys (presumed, see discovery-gaps). Gates are local: Husky pre-commit and pre-push, and repo:check (format, lint, types, vars, skills, openapi check, agent compat). Cron: vercel.json runs /api/v1/admin/send-digest daily at 08:00 UTC.

QA repo (this one), workflows in .github/workflows/:

WorkflowTriggerWhat it runs
build.yml (TestBuild)pull_request to mainenv check, types, lint, playwright test --list
smoke.ymlcron 02:00 UTC daily, manualtest:smoke, then test:sync to Xray, Allure artifacts
regression.ymlcron 00:00 UTC daily, manualtest:integration then E2E, test:sync, Allure published to gh-pages
sanity.ymlmanualsanity subset, test:sync, Allure

All suites target TEST_ENV=staging by default and read credentials from repository secrets.

Discovery gaps

  • Could not verify how deploys are triggered (Git integration vs CLI): only .vercel/project.json and vercel.json exist.
  • Could not verify any rollback procedure or Vercel/Supabase region; not in repo.
  • No rate limiting found for general API routes (references exist only in the magic-link and check-email contracts, Jira client and error envelope); limits not measured.
  • No APM, error tracker or alerting found.
  • OAuth provider setup (GitHub, Google) lives in the Supabase dashboard; not verifiable from code.
  • Migration ledger row count not readable: the QA read-only role has no access to supabase_migrations.
  • Frontend test-id convention and browser support targets not investigated.
  • Staging /qa is a hint, cross-checked only for stack and auth methods.
  • Production environment is not declared in .agents/project.yaml (the qa env is also null).
